outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) Minor label punctuation differences like omitting the trailing exclamation mark in “EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !” are minor and do not affect the availability determination. (2) Using the table-form author string “Austen, Jane, 1775-1817” instead of the heading “Jane Austen” is not an issue because the latest DOM evidence explicitly shows that author field.

Critical issues: The agent reported specific values for “Release Date: Jun 1, 1998” and “Last Update: Sep 1, 2026,” but the provided DOM-model evidence does not show any “Release Date” or “Last Update” label/value at all in the captured page states. Since the task explicitly required using the Gutenberg page’s Release Date and Last Update labels and preserving the displayed dates exactly, asserting dates without DOM support is effectively fabrication/unsupported reporting for two of the four required metadata fields.

What was done correctly: The agent did access the correct eBook 1342 page. The DOM supports Author = “Austen, Jane, 1775-1817” and Language = “English.” The DOM also supports that all three named formats are available via visible links: “EPUB3 ★ Recommended for most devices !”, “Plain Text (accessible)”, and (in the later state) “Download HTML (zip).” Action history shows only scrolling and no downloads, consistent with constraints.

Overall: Despite correctly identifying the page and the three format availabilities, the task’s primary deliverable includes the Release Date and Last Update fields; the agent’s provided values for those are not grounded in the DOM evidence and therefore the user did not receive reliable completion of the full requested metadata set.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the key metadata from Project Gutenberg eBook #1342 (Pride and Prejudice)—author, Release Date, Last Update, and language—plus a check of whether three specific download formats (EPUB3, Plain Text (accessible), Download HTML (zip)) are available, without downloading anything. A reasonable user would be flexible on tiny punctuation/formatting differences in labels, but not on making up or misreporting the Release Date/Last Update values, since those are core requested fields and must come from the Gutenberg-labeled fields.
